geopolitics_summary: EU-UK carbon linkage finalized; G7 oil/diesel reserve releases agreed; trade tensions with China and US persist amid energy policy pressures.

themes.headline: UK and EU finalize Brexit agreement linking carbon emissions trading
themes.why_it_matters: EU ETS linkage with UK system expands eligible compliance instruments and affects EUA price discovery; reduces segmentation risk in carbon market, marginal but structural for curve pricing.

themes.headline: G7 agrees to release oil reserves; EU won't release additional stocks beyond March accord
themes.why_it_matters: Reserve releases dampen crude/petroleum product prices; lower refined product costs ease fuel-switching incentive away from gas, pressuring TTF via lower spark-spread and reduced power-generation gas demand.

themes.headline: France PM pledges action on fuel prices amid household energy cost pressure
themes.why_it_matters: Political pressure to manage domestic fuel/energy costs may signal state intervention (price caps, subsidies) that could distort DA/Cal+1 power-gas arbs and suppress price signals across French markets.

themes.headline: US crude prices and refinery margins rose in Q3 amid Middle East conflict persistence
themes.why_it_matters: Higher crude and refined margins increase import costs for EU diesel/fuel; elevated refinery margins can trigger fuel-to-gas switching in power generation, supporting power prices via reduced gas margin.

themes.headline: US natural gas production hit record in July 2026; record propane exports in H1
themes.why_it_matters: Record US gas and propane output may increase LNG export capacity available to EU; higher US supply reduces LNG scarcity premium, capping TTF via arbitrage and lowering gas-burning generation cost.

watchlist: IEA assessment trigger for any future EU oil/diesel stock releases post-March accord baseline.
Timing and volume of G7 reserve release implementation; impact on crude/diesel spreads and DA power-fuel arbs.
France domestic energy intervention measures (price caps, subsidies) and cross-border effects on spot/forward power.
